body:
### Goal
Add a command line option to allow setuid binaries to still work in bubblewrap environments.

### But why?!
Bubblewrap is not only useful to sandbox executables, but also for running them in a shim environment with a different view of the filesystem. NixOS for example extensively uses bubblewrap to build FHS environments in which a regular FHS compliant filetree is visible.

In most cases this works fine, but in some cases, especially with development environments, `setuid` binaries are required to work inside these FHS environments. An FHS environment on NixOS is not meant to be a security shelter, but rather just a tool to get more applications running.

### How
The default behavior doesn't change, bubblewrap still by default denies new privileges, but a flag has been added `--unsafe-new-privileges`, which explicitly doesn't drop the `PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS` capability.

This pr refactors `TscModule ` formerly (`TypeScriptModule `), it aims to introduce the features:

- [x] `package` RootModule with TscModule
- [x] relative paths
- [x] esm support; use swc-core for compiling

Key changes:
- `compile` task has been modified, these modifications:
    - change how sources, mod-sources, resources and generated sources are grouped, allowing for the use of relative paths 
    - these changes also taking into consideration `RootModule` use, the top level src feature now works along side `TscModule`

    - The restructuring also consequentially fixes the need for `TscModule` to violate the new `writing to path during execution phase` restrictions. Clarifies that in Isthmus, `EIP-7685` is disabled, and by side-effect, `EIP-6110`, `EIP-7002`, and `EIP-7251` are disabled as well.

This implies that the OP Stack execution layer should skip these system calls entirely, as to not add needless computation to the block processing routine or treat the `EIP-7685`-dependent contracts introduced by L1's Pectra fork as in-protocol.

author: karllark
body:
This add the option to have a repeating boundary condition for photons that would normally exit in the x or y directions.  The option is in the "Run" section of the parameter file (i.e., add the line "repeat_boundary_xy=1").  This option only will work correctly for models that fully fill the main grid - no cells with -0.5 indicating the edge of the model has been reached.   The slab geometry meets this criteria.   The file geometry can meet this criteria if the file is setup with no -0.5 values.

The repeating xy boundary will cause longer run times as the photon trajectories are longer.  These run times can be *much* longer depending on the optical depths of the model.  And low may mean longer than high, depending on the geometry. 

Closes #38.

author: kaladay
body:
Simplify scripts and make workflows conditional.

The workflows need to conditionally run.
Utilize the GitHub Actions output variables to transfer data between jobs.
This enables a job to use the results from another job to determine if it should be run on not.

Use Bash functions and guard clauses to simplify the script.
- The `${result}` variable is defined in the `main()` and can be directly modified without having to return with a code.
- Reduce the number of return statements.
- The `main()` should still return with any error codes (which is a bug being fixed because `0` was always being returned).
- Both commit and push should only operate if there are changes.
- Add `SYNC_SNAPSHOT_RESULT` environment variable to designate the name of the file used to store the results status.

A file for the `SYNC_SNAPSHOT_RESULT` is used to make using the GitHub Actions Workflow simpler to write.
A `cat` command can be easily called by the Workflow to populate the variable.

Update the `populate_release.sh` script in a similar way as is done for `sync_snapshot.sh`.

The workflow steps must have IDs in order to properly use output variables.

Have git ignore the `results.txt` file.

see: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/writing-workflows/choosing-what-your-workflow-does/workflow-commands-for-github-actions#setting-an-output-parameter
